title: Case studies
text: These studies look back at the largest up and down days since the SpaceX listing on June 12, 2026. Each one applies the journal’s method to a day whose outcome is already known: what moved, which channel drove it, what happened over the following five trading days, and what the episode teaches.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Observation

SPCX rose 19.6% to $192.50, about 43% above its $135 offer price, on its second day of trading.
SPY gained 1.76% and QQQ 3.14%. The space group averaged +7.3% (RKLB +6.7%) and semiconductors +4.4%.
Crude oil fell 4.9% to $80.75 and XOM lost 4.1%. The VIX fell 8.4% to 16.2.
Defensive and healthcare groups were slightly negative.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Mechanism
Two separate things happened on the same day.
SpaceX: the flows channel.

Only about 5% of the company was sold in the offering, so the tradable supply was small.
Index providers had announced fast inclusion, so funds that track those indexes were expected to become forced buyers.
Heavy retail demand met that small supply, and the price rose without any new information about cash flows.

The broad market: the risk premium channel.

A reported US-Iran deal lowered the odds of an oil supply disruption.
Oil fell, which eased inflation pressure and lowered the premium investors demanded for risk.
Energy producers fell with oil while growth and semiconductor names led.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPCX fell 18.9%, QQQ fell 4.0% and SPY fell 2.6%. SpaceX gave back more than the whole second-day gain within a week.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Lesson
A price set by scarce supply and forced buyers is not a statement about value. When a move has no cash-flow news behind it, the question to ask is who had to buy and whether they are finished. Peers moved in sympathy on the way up and offered no protection on the way down.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Observation

NVDA fell 14.01% to $125.53. SMH fell 10.6%, QQQ 5.67% and SPY 3.64%.
The VIX rose 26.2% to 35.9.
Bonds rallied: TLT +1.37%, and the 10-year yield fell to 4.91%.
Gold did not: GLD fell 3.67%. Defensives (+1.1%) and healthcare (+0.9%) rose.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk premium, amplified by flows.

Reuters reported that the SEC was examining Nvidia’s accounting.
An accounting question makes reported earnings less reliable, so investors demand a higher return to hold the stock.
The price fell without any change to revenue forecasts; the company had reported record results three days earlier.
Because Nvidia is one of the largest weights in the major indexes, its fall pulled the benchmarks down with it.
Gold falling on a day when bonds rose points to investors selling what they could to raise cash.

The gold side of this day is analysed in the journal entry of the same date.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
What happened next
Too recent to assess. The outcome is being tracked in the live journal.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Lesson
Good earnings do not protect a stock when the question is whether the earnings can be trusted. Also, a safe asset does not always behave like one: in a forced selloff, the most liquid holdings are sold first, whatever their fundamentals.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Observation

MSFT rose 15.51%, its largest one-day gain since 2008. META fell 7.95% on the same day.
AMD gained 13.0% and SMH 6.9%. SPY rose 1.68% and QQQ 3.30%.
Healthcare (-2.4%) and defensives (-1.6%) fell. The VIX dropped 17.3% to 17.1.
The 10-year yield ended at 4.66%, slightly higher on the day.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows.
Two companies in the same industry reported on the same evening and moved in opposite directions.

Microsoft showed cloud growth above expectations and did not raise its capital spending plans.
Meta missed on earnings, raised its spending forecast and reported a sharp fall in free cash flow.
The market rewarded evidence that AI spending was turning into revenue, and penalized spending without it.
Semiconductors rallied because Microsoft’s result supported continued demand for AI hardware.
Defensives were sold to fund the move back into growth.

Yields did not fall, so this was not a discount-rate rally. It was driven by earnings.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days MSFT rose a further 10.8%, META recovered 9.4% and SPY rose 3.6%.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Lesson
Markets price the surprise relative to expectations, not the level. When a theme is under doubt, the dispersion between companies inside it carries more information than the average. The question the market asked of AI spending that day was specific: where is the revenue?

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Observation

SPY fell 1.54% and QQQ 2.04%. NVDA fell 3.55%.
Crude oil rose 6.6% to $84.46. XOM gained 2.4% and the commodity group was the only one clearly positive.
Long Treasuries fell too: TLT lost 1.65%. The VIX rose 13.5% to 20.7.
The weakest groups were space (-6.4%), semiconductors (-4.2%) and cyclicals (-3.2%, with CAT -6.9%).

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk-free rate, with a cash-flow effect on cyclicals.

An Iranian missile attack on US forces raised the risk of lost oil supply.
Oil jumped, which raised expected inflation on the day of a Federal Reserve decision.
Higher expected inflation raised the odds of rate increases, so bond prices fell and yields rose.
A higher discount rate hit the longest-duration equities hardest: space and semiconductors.
Higher fuel and input costs hit cyclicals through their margins.

The signature of an inflation shock is that stocks and bonds fall on the same day. In a growth scare, bonds would have rallied.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPY rose 5.5%, NVDA 15.4% and MSFT 24.8%. Oil eased, and Microsoft’s results after that day’s close changed the subject.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Lesson
An oil supply shock can be identified from three things moving together: energy up, bonds down, cyclicals down. It can also fade within days if no supply is actually lost. Before extrapolating a geopolitical move, check whether barrels have been removed from the market or only the fear of it.

title: Hot inflation, new tariffs, and an AI selloff: the three days before Thanksgiving
text: Written on the afternoon of Wednesday, November 25, before the close and before the Thanksgiving holiday. It covers Monday to Wednesday. The analysis and the prediction were written before Wednesday’s close; the figures in the table were updated to closing prices afterwards.

Monday is analysed in the entry of November 23 and Tuesday in the entry of November 24.
Also on Wednesday: CoreWeave and Nebius each fell by double digits. Outside AI the market rose: small caps (IWM) +0.6%, cyclicals +0.9%, rate-sensitive shares +0.8%, and Treasury bond funds gained.
Over the three sessions, from the November 20 close: Nvidia +18.9%, SMH +5.6%, SPY +3.9%, GLD +1.4%, TLT +1.0%.


The PCE report in detail

What it is. The personal consumption expenditures price index, published by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. The Federal Reserve’s 2% inflation goal is defined on this measure.
Headline: 3.8% over the year in October, up from 3.6% in September.
Core (excluding food and energy): 3.3% over the year, above the 3.2% forecast and the highest in three years. Core rose 0.3% over the month.
Released with it: third-quarter GDP revised up to 4.3%.
Why it matters. Inflation is almost twice the target and rising, and growth is strong. It was the last major inflation release before the Fed decides on December 9, and markets priced a rate increase at above 90%.



The tariff proposal

What was announced. Proposed tariffs of about 20% on China, the European Union, and 12 other trading partners, following an eight-month investigation into excess manufacturing capacity.
Status. Proposed, not imposed. There is a public comment period, and January is the earliest start.
Does Congress have to approve? No. The trade law being used lets the executive branch impose tariffs after an investigation. The risks to the plan are court challenges and legislation from Congress, which would need enough votes to survive a veto.
Background. The Supreme Court struck down the earlier, broader tariffs in February 2026. Tariffs on China under this older law survived court challenges in the past.



What I confirmed, and what I refined
Confirmed by the data

Nvidia came back on Monday and has faded since, while keeping most of the gain.
Memory stocks are falling hard, and SKHY is near its low.
A rate increase is expected.
When people rush into Treasuries, the yield goes down.
Gold has come back a little: GLD is 1.4% above its November 20 close.

Refined after checking the numbers

Inflation: 2% is the Fed’s target. The current reading is 3.8%, which is why a rate increase is expected.
TLT: it is a fund holding long Treasuries, so its number is a price. TLT rising means long-term yields falling. The 10-year and the longer maturities moved the same way this week.
“Interest rates”: there are two. The expected policy rate went up. Market yields on longer bonds went down.
Gold’s path: it was not a straight recovery. It rose Monday, fell Tuesday, and made a new 52-week low on Wednesday morning before recovering.
The dollar: it is at a high level, but it did not rise further after Monday.
Tariffs: they were proposed, and are not yet in force.

Arrows show cause and effect on the day. A higher policy rate also weighs on gold directly and supports the dollar.
The puzzle: hot inflation usually lifts long-term yields. Today the safety bid from falling stocks was stronger, so yields fell.
Two rates moved in opposite directions: the expected policy rate went up, the 10-year market yield went down.
1. THE NEWS (NOVEMBER 25)
2. WHAT CHANGES
3. EQUITIES
4. WHERE THE MONEY GOES
HOW TO READ IT


Three shocks on one day

Inflation and growth data (risk-free rate channel). Hot core PCE with strong GDP makes a December rate increase close to certain.
Tariff proposals (cash flows, and inflation). My reasoning: tariffs raise the cost of imported parts and goods, so profit margins fall, and global companies are hit most. Two things to add: other countries can retaliate against US exporters, and higher import prices feed inflation, which keeps rates high. Semiconductors are exposed on both sides because their supply chains cross many borders.
AI-specific doubts (cash flows). Analysts cut their outlook for memory prices and downgraded Micron, on top of the wider question of whether debt-funded AI spending will pay off. My own view is that AI keeps raising demand for memory. The market’s worry is about supply and prices, not about demand.



How the six factors connect

Policy rate, up. Hot inflation raises the expected Fed rate.
AI equities, down. Their value rests on profits far in the future, so a higher discount rate hurts them most, and AI also had its own bad news. Semiconductors averaged -6.0% on Tuesday and -1.8% on Wednesday.
Space, down then up. The space group fell 7.4% on Tuesday with the other long-duration names, then rose 4.0% on Wednesday, led by ASTS. Space and AI are the two most volatile groups I track.
Dividend, defensive and cyclical shares, up. Their cash arrives sooner, so they are less sensitive to the discount rate, and money rotates into them when growth stocks are sold.
Treasuries, bought; long yields, down. The selloff sends money into bonds for safety. Prices rise, so the 10-year yield falls and TLT rises.
Dollar, flat at a high level. Higher short-term rates support it. Falling long-term yields hold it back, because foreign investors earn less on US bonds than they did the day before.
Gold, a new low and then a recovery. Lower yields with higher inflation should lift gold, and that logic is sound for long-term real yields. In the morning two stronger forces worked against it: a higher expected policy rate raises the cost of holding an asset that pays nothing, and investors with stock losses sold gold to raise cash. As stocks recovered, the selling eased and gold ended higher.
Oil, down Monday, up since. WTI fell 4.5% on Monday and has risen a little over 2% on each day since, to about $84. Rising oil adds to inflation pressure. Monday’s fall was a supply story, not a result of the Nvidia news.



Points to study further

Hot inflation normally lifts long-term yields. On Wednesday they fell, because the safety bid was stronger. A rising policy rate with a falling long yield also says the market expects tighter policy to slow growth later.
Gold rose in the November 5 selloff, fell on November 20 and on Tuesday, and on Wednesday fell and then recovered within the day. Its behaviour seems to depend on whether investors are being forced to sell.
Space rose on Wednesday while AI fell. My rule that space follows AI on rate days did not hold, so company news inside the group needs checking.
A strong dollar is supposed to weigh on other markets. Korea fell more than 6% on Wednesday, but memory chips led that, not the currency.

title: Hot inflation, new tariffs, and an AI selloff: the three days before Thanksgiving
text:
Quant research and trading topics
Each topic starts from something the market did that my framework did not fully expect. A research topic turns that surprise into a rule that can be tested on past data before any money is involved. The trading uses are conditional: they describe how the result would be used if the test supports it, and none is a recommendation.
1. Sensitivity to inflation surprises

Question: How much does each group move for every tenth of a point by which core inflation beats or misses the forecast?
Why it may matter: Markets react to the surprise, not the level. Core PCE came in 0.1 above forecast and the Nasdaq opened down more than 4%. Knowing each group’s usual reaction separates a normal move from an unusual one.
How I can test it in this journal: Build a table of PCE and CPI release dates with the forecast and the actual figure. Regress each group’s return on that day against the surprise to get an inflation sensitivity for each group.
Trading use, if it holds: Position sizes and hedges going into a data release.

2. Overnight moves and intraday recovery

Question: After a large fall at the open, how often does the market recover during the session?
Why it may matter: The Nasdaq was down more than 4% near the open and QQQ closed down 0.7%. If bad news is over-priced at the open, the rest of the day leans the other way.
How I can test it in this journal: Add opening prices to the data script, which the data source already provides. Split each day’s return into overnight (previous close to open) and intraday (open to close), and study intraday returns after large overnight gaps.
Trading use, if it holds: Whether to act at the open or wait: one of the most studied patterns in equities.

3. When bonds protect a stock portfolio

Question: In which conditions do Treasuries rise when stocks fall?
Why it may matter: On Wednesday TLT rose 0.9% as stocks fell, even with hot inflation. In earlier inflation scares, stocks and bonds fell together. The answer decides how much protection bonds give.
How I can test it in this journal: Compute a rolling 20-day correlation between SPY and TLT, and compare it across days driven by inflation news, growth fears, and company news, using the tags on my entries.
Trading use, if it holds: The mix of stocks and bonds in a portfolio, which is the first decision an asset allocator makes.

4. Option prices after a shock

Question: After the VIX rises above 25, is the volatility that follows higher or lower than options had priced in?
Why it may matter: It decides whether buying options after a shock is good value. This bears directly on the first row of my strategy notes.
How I can test it in this journal: Compare the VIX on each such day with the volatility SPY actually realized over the following 21 trading days, using the price file.
Trading use, if it holds: Choosing between buying an option and holding the underlying fund.

5. Tariff announcements

Question: Do stocks react more on the day a tariff is proposed or on the day it takes effect?
Why it may matter: The tariffs announced on Wednesday are proposals with a January start at the earliest. If most of the reaction comes at the proposal, the later date matters less.
How I can test it in this journal: List past tariff proposal and effective dates, and compare the returns of semiconductors and international funds on each kind of day.
Trading use, if it holds: Timing exposure to trade-sensitive groups around known policy dates.

title: SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report

Mechanism


Market: the risk-free rate channel. Lower oil, lower inflation pressure, lower yields, so stocks and bonds rose together.
SpaceX: positioning. Buyers bid the stock up 9% before knowing the numbers.
That raised the bar: the report now had to beat the higher expectation built into the price.

Right. SPCX fell 13.6% the next day: revenue beat expectations but capital spending rose sharply.

GLD closed at $322.87 on Nov 20, down from $369.36 on Nov 10 (-12.6%) and from $355.45 on Nov 13 (-9.2% on the week).

Over the same week the 10-year Treasury yield fell from about 5.15% to 4.92%, and the 10-year real yield was nearly flat (2.91% to 2.88%).

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Mechanism

My first explanation: the risk-free rate channel.

Gold pays no interest.
When real yields are high, holding gold means giving up more income.
Investors shift from gold to bonds, and gold falls.

Test against the data: yields fell last week, so this channel predicts gold flat or higher. Gold fell 9%. The rate story explains the decline since January, but not this week.
Revised explanation: the flows channel.

Equities fell sharply and volatility spiked.
Leveraged investors faced margin calls and needed cash.
They sold liquid assets, including gold, regardless of its fundamentals.
Evidence: double the normal volume, gold’s worst day matching the equity market’s worst day, and silver falling harder than gold.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Prediction


55% probability that GLD closes above $322.87 on Nov 30 (five trading days).
Reasoning: forced selling ends when the selling pressure in equities eases, even if yields do not move.
Wrong if GLD closes at or below $322.87 on Nov 30.
What I will watch: if the VIX falls and gold still declines, the flows explanation is wrong and rates or the dollar matter more than I think.
Disclosure: I hold a small position in GLD.

title: The day Huang returned: a 31% rebound in Nvidia and what it did to every market
text:
NoteWritten two sessions later



This entry was written on November 25, after the next two sessions were known. It analyses Monday, November 23 in hindsight, carries no scored prediction, and is excluded from the scored record.

title: The day Huang returned: a 31% rebound in Nvidia and what it did to every market
text:
Observation


The news

Nvidia announced that its board had voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and chief executive, effective immediately. He had resigned on November 13.

One piece of company news removed one risk. It did not answer the wider doubt about the return on AI spending.
Gold rose with stocks, the mirror image of November 20, which supports the forced-selling explanation.
Oil moved the same day for its own reasons. Two things falling or rising together is not proof that one caused the other.
1. THE NEWS (NOVEMBER 23)
2. WHAT CHANGES
3. EQUITIES
4. WHERE THE MONEY GOES
HOW TO READ IT


The chain

Risk premium, down. The selloff of November 20 came from doubt about Nvidia’s leadership and accounts. Reinstating the chief executive removed the leadership part of that doubt, so investors demanded less extra return to hold the stock.
Flows, reversed. The market was oversold. Short sellers had to buy back, and buyers who had stepped aside returned, which turned a repricing into a 31% day.
AI and space equities, up most. They had fallen most and are the most sensitive to changes in risk appetite. They are the two most volatile groups I track.
Yields: short end up, long end steady. With the crisis easing, the Federal Reserve is freer to raise rates in December, so short-term yields rose. The 10-year barely moved.
Dollar, up. Higher expected US short-term rates raised the return on dollars.
Gold, up. This is the mirror image of November 20. Gold fell that day because investors sold it to cover losses. When the forced selling stopped, gold rebounded. It supports the flows explanation in my November 20 entry.
Oil, down 4.5%. It fell on the same day, and it is worth keeping separate: reports put it down to supply, not to the Nvidia news. Two things moving on the same day are not necessarily connected.



Points to study further

Gold and the dollar rose together, which is unusual. Gold was recovering from forced selling while the dollar was responding to rate expectations: two different causes on one day.
The 10-year yield barely moved on a day of very good news, and it fell two days later on a day of hot inflation. In this market the direction of long-term yields seems to follow demand for safety more than the inflation data.

title: The day Huang returned: a 31% rebound in Nvidia and what it did to every market
text:
What happened next

Tuesday, November 24: Nvidia fell 5.9% to $155.38, semiconductors averaged -6.0%, and the space group -7.4%. QQQ lost 2.0% while defensives and healthcare rose, and the Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time. See the entry of November 24.
Wednesday, November 25: hot inflation data, new tariff proposals, and more selling in AI stocks. See the entry of November 25.
Over the three sessions: Nvidia kept an 18.9% gain from the November 20 close, SMH 5.6%, and SPY 3.9%.

title: The day Huang returned: a 31% rebound in Nvidia and what it did to every market
text:
Lesson
One piece of company news can remove one risk. It cannot answer a different question. The return of the chief executive settled who runs Nvidia. It did not settle whether AI spending will earn a return, what the investigations will find, or how high rates will go. A relief rally is as large as the fear it removes, and it fades when the remaining questions come back into view.
For my own method: check the cause of each move separately before connecting them.

title: The day Huang returned: a 31% rebound in Nvidia and what it did to every market
text:
Quant research and trading topics
Each topic starts from something the market did that my framework did not fully expect. A research topic turns that surprise into a rule that can be tested on past data before any money is involved. The trading uses are conditional: they describe how the result would be used if the test supports it, and none is a recommendation.
1. How much of a relief rally is kept

Question: After a single-day gain above 10% in a stock, what share of the gain remains after 5 and 20 trading days?
Why it may matter: A jump can come from new information, which tends to last, or from short sellers buying back, which tends to fade. Nvidia gave back 5.9 points of its 31.5 the next day.
How I can test it in this journal: Extend the price download to five years. Find every day with a move above 10% in the watchlist, and measure each stock’s return relative to its group over the following 5 and 20 days.
Trading use, if it holds: The result says whether to follow a large move or wait for it to settle.

2. Sympathy moves beyond normal sensitivity

Question: When the sector leader jumps, do peers that rise more than their usual link to the leader implies give back the excess?
Why it may matter: On a day like this, buyers lift the whole group without distinguishing between companies. The space group rose 8.8% on news about a chipmaker.
How I can test it in this journal: Estimate each semiconductor and space ticker’s sensitivity to Nvidia over the previous 60 days. On the shock day, compute the excess move (actual minus expected) and check whether it reverses over the next three days.
Trading use, if it holds: A pair trade between names that over-reacted and names that under-reacted.

3. Gold as a gauge of forced selling

Question: Is gold falling together with stocks a sign that investors are being forced to sell, and does its recovery mark the end of that selling?
Why it may matter: Gold fell with stocks on November 20 and rebounded with them on November 23. In ordinary stress the two move in opposite directions.
How I can test it in this journal: Compute a rolling five-day correlation between GLD and SPY. Mark the days when both fell more than 2%, and study SPY over the following five days.
Trading use, if it holds: A flag for capitulation: evidence that a selloff is driven by forced sellers, not by new information.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Mechanism


Channel: the risk-free rate.
Higher oil raises expected inflation.
Higher expected inflation raises the chance of Fed rate increases, so yields rise and bond prices fall.
A higher discount rate hurts long-duration stocks the most.
Cyclicals were hit separately through higher fuel and input costs.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Scoring


Wrong. SPY rose 5.5% over the five days.
The broken link: oil did not stay high. It fell 10.9% over the same five days as tensions cooled.
A second force arrived that I had not weighed: Microsoft reported that evening and rose 15.5% the next day.
Lesson: the mechanism was sound, but it depended on oil staying up. State the condition in the prediction, and check the earnings calendar before predicting an index.

The index barely moved (SPY -0.5%) while the groups inside it moved a lot in opposite directions.
Money rotated between stocks instead of leaving for bonds, which is why yields stayed flat.
Gold fell with no help from the dollar or yields: on this day it traded with the AI names, not as a safe asset.
1. THE NEWS (NOVEMBER 24)
2. WHAT CHANGES
3. EQUITIES
4. THE OTHER MARKETS
HOW TO READ IT


The chain

Cash flows, down for AI hardware. A weaker outlook for memory prices lowered expected profits for memory makers, and the worry spread to the rest of the chip group.
Flows: profit-taking. After a 31% day, buyers from Monday sold part of their gains.
Rotation, not flight. Money moved from AI and space into healthcare and defensive shares. The index barely moved and the VIX was flat, so this was a change of leadership inside the market, not a rush for the exit.
Yields, unchanged. Because money stayed in stocks, there was no surge of buying in Treasuries.
Dollar, down. It gave back Monday’s gain as the 10-year yield eased slightly.
Gold, down. It fell 2.3% with a weaker dollar and steady yields, both of which normally help it. On this day gold traded with the AI names, not as a safe asset.
Oil, up. It recovered part of Monday’s fall, for reasons of its own.



Points to study further

Space fell more than semiconductors, though the news was about memory chips. The two groups seem to share the same investors more than the same business.
Gold has now fallen on a day of forced selling (November 20) and on a day of rotation (November 24). The common factor may be selling by investors who hold both gold and AI stocks.

Lesson
A flat index can hide a large move. The information on this day was in the gap between groups, not in the benchmark. I should read the group table on the Dashboard before the headline number.

title: The relief rally fades: a rotation out of AI as the Dow passes 50,000
text:
Quant research and trading topics
Each topic starts from something the market did that my framework did not fully expect. A research topic turns that surprise into a rule that can be tested on past data before any money is involved. The trading uses are conditional: they describe how the result would be used if the test supports it, and none is a recommendation.
1. Rotation and dispersion

Question: When the index is flat but the groups inside it move far apart, does the gap keep widening or close again?
Why it may matter: On this day SPY fell 0.5% while semiconductors fell 6.0% and healthcare rose 2.7%. A flat index can hide a large trade between groups.
How I can test it in this journal: From the Dashboard’s 11 groups, compute each day’s dispersion (the standard deviation of group returns) and a spread (defensive and healthcare minus semiconductors and space). Check whether today’s spread predicts the spread over the next one and five days.
Trading use, if it holds: A long-short position between groups, which does not depend on the direction of the market.

2. Information crossing time zones

Question: Does a large move in US memory stocks predict the move in Korean memory stocks at their next session?
Why it may matter: Micron fell 11% in New York on Tuesday, and SK hynix fell 11% in Seoul on Wednesday. News travels with the clock, and the second market may react too much or too little.
How I can test it in this journal: Add MU and a Korea fund (EWY) to the watchlist. Regress EWY’s next-day return on Micron’s return, and compare how much of the move was already priced during US hours.
Trading use, if it holds: A lead-lag signal between markets, sized by how reliably the second market follows the first.

3. Relative strength inside a falling group

Question: Do stocks that fall less than their group on a bad day go on to outperform the group?
Why it may matter: Nvidia fell 5.9% while other chip stocks fell a median 9%. Holding up better under pressure may signal stronger demand for the stock.
How I can test it in this journal: Each day, rank the semiconductor tickers by their return minus the group average. Track the next five days’ relative return of the top and bottom names.
Trading use, if it holds: A within-sector pair: the stronger name against the weaker one, which removes most sector risk.

How to read the charts

Five-day return is the average close-to-close return of the tickers in each group. Blue bars are gains and orange bars are losses.
Volatility is the average annualized volatility of the tickers in each group, measured from daily returns over the last 20 trading days.
Read them together: a group with a large loss and high volatility is under stress; a small move with low volatility is calm.
Macro series are left out because a yield or an index level is not comparable with a tradable price.

1d % and 5d % are close-to-close returns over one and five trading days.
vs 20d / 50d / 200d avg % show how far the latest close sits above (positive) or below (negative) its 20-, 50- and 200-day moving average: the short-, medium- and long-term trend.
trend is a rule-based label: Up when the close is above the 50-day average and the 50-day is above the 200-day; Down when both are reversed; Mixed otherwise. It describes the current trend. It is not a forecast and not a recommendation to buy or sell.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Observation

SPY fell 4.41%, QQQ 6.49% and IWM 4.59%.
NVDA fell 9.26%, AMD 17.26% and SMH 11.2%. The space group averaged -12.4%.
The VIX rose 69.7% to 28.2.
Safe assets behaved normally: TLT +0.21%, GLD +0.81%, and the 10-year yield fell to 4.84%.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows and the risk premium, amplified by flows.

The midterm elections produced a sweep for the Democrats.
Investors feared new regulation of data-center development, which would slow the AI build-out.
A slower build-out means lower expected revenue for chipmakers and their suppliers, so those stocks were repriced.
A volatility jump of that size typically forces strategies that target a fixed level of risk to cut positions, which would have added to the selling. I have not verified positioning data for this day.

Yields fell on the day and growth stocks still collapsed. That rules out the discount rate as the cause: this was about expected cash flows and uncertainty.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPY recovered 3.3% and QQQ 6.4%, after several brokerages argued that extreme regulation was unlikely. NVDA fell a further 8.5% for reasons specific to the company.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Lesson
The market priced a risk, not a law. Policy shocks tend to be priced at their worst case on the first day and revised as the realistic range becomes clearer. It is also worth comparing gold here with November 20: on this day gold rose, a normal flight to safety; two weeks later it fell with stocks, which pointed to forced selling.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Observation

QQQ fell 3.47% and SPY 1.77%.
AMD fell 10.88%, SMH 6.98% and NVDA 4.22%. The space group averaged -6.8%.
Defensives (+1.3%) and healthcare (+0.5%) rose. TLT gained 0.43% and the 10-year yield ended at 4.93%.
GLD fell 3.47%. The VIX rose 12.9% to 19.4.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows.

Intel fell 28.6% after its results, and Amazon’s report added to concern about the cost of AI infrastructure.
Investors questioned whether the industry’s capital spending would earn an adequate return.
That doubt was applied to the whole hardware supply chain, so semiconductors were repriced together.
Money rotated into defensives and bonds, which is an orderly move away from one theme, not a rush for cash.

The dispersion inside the sector is informative: NVDA fell less than half as much as AMD, so investors were still ranking companies and not selling the group indiscriminately.
Open question. Gold fell 3.5% on a day when bonds rose. A safe asset falling alongside equities can indicate selling to cover losses elsewhere. I would need positioning data to confirm it.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days QQQ fell a further 5.0%, NVDA 8.8% and AMD 11.0%. The selling continued.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Lesson
Compare this with July 29. A geopolitical shock reversed within days because the feared event did not happen. A repricing based on doubts about cash flows persisted, because nothing arrived to answer the doubt. The cause of a selloff says a lot about how long it lasts.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Observation

SPY rose 2.37%, QQQ 3.54% and IWM 3.23%.
AMD gained 13.26% and the space group averaged +11.5%.
NVDA fell 4.27% to $178.67, the only large semiconductor name to decline.
Crude oil fell 4.4% to $86.85 and the VIX dropped 22.3% to 19.9.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Mechanism
The market: the risk-free rate and a falling risk premium.

Oil fell, which eased inflation concern.
Analysts argued the previous week’s selloff had overstated the regulatory risk.
Buyers returned to the names that had fallen most.

Nvidia: company-specific risk premium.

The company said it was examining claims of a foreign intelligence effort connected to its chief executive.
That raised governance and key-person risk for one company only.
Investors demanded a higher return to hold it, so it fell while its peers rallied.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days NVDA fell a further 12.6% as the chief executive resigned, while SPY lost 1.7%.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Lesson
When the leading stock of a sector diverges from the sector on company news, the divergence is the information. Governance events are rarely resolved in one disclosure, so the first day’s move is usually not the full repricing.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Observation

SPY rose 1.80% to a record close and QQQ rose 3.40%.
Crude oil fell 5.7% to $75.77. TLT gained 0.77% and the 10-year yield ended at 4.63%.
SPCX rose 9.43% to $125.33 ahead of its first report as a public company, still below its $135 offer price.
Space (+8.1%), semiconductors (+4.9%) and cyclicals (+2.8%) led. Healthcare was the only negative group.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk-free rate, plus cash flows from earnings.
This was the mirror image of July 29.

Hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil lower.
Lower oil eased inflation pressure, so bond yields fell.
A lower discount rate lifted long-duration equities, and stocks and bonds rose together.
Strong results and guidance from industrial and software companies added a cash-flow reason to buy.

SpaceX: positioning ahead of an event. The stock rose 9% before the numbers were known, which raised the bar the report had to clear.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
What happened next
SpaceX reported revenue above expectations after the close, but capital spending rose sharply and the stock fell 13.6% the next day. SPY was flat over the following five trading days.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Lesson
A run-up into an event is a bet on the outcome, and it leaves less room for a good result to be rewarded. The reaction also repeated the July 30 pattern: revenue alone was not enough when spending surprised on the high side.

text:

title: About
text: Market Journal is a daily research journal written by Blaire (Meina) Bian.

title: About
text:
What it is
Each entry takes one market move and works through it in four steps:

Observation: what moved, by how much, relative to the benchmark.
Mechanism: which channel drove it (cash flows, the risk-free rate, the risk premium, or flows) and the causal chain behind it.
Prediction: a testable call with a deadline and a probability.
Scoring: whether the call was right, and which link in the reasoning held or broke.

Every entry is committed to version control, so each prediction carries a timestamp that precedes its outcome. Entries dated before November 20, 2026 are retrospective exercises, labelled as written in hindsight and excluded from the scored record.

title: About
text:
Why
To build calibrated, mechanism-level judgment about how macroeconomic, policy, and company-level shocks transmit into asset prices. The journal is paired with a simulated portfolio so that each view is tested with a position.

title: About
text:
More detail
The full framework, including the factor map and the rules for the simulated portfolio, is in the project README.
This is a personal learning project. Nothing here is investment advice.
